questions.question: What is a Kriti?
questions.expectedAnswer: A Kriti is a mature Carnatic composition that combines music, lyrics, devotion and the character of a raga.

questions.question: Why is a Kriti important in Carnatic music?
questions.expectedAnswer: A Kriti is important because it expresses musical beauty, devotion, poetry and raga depth.

questions.question: State one difference between a Geetham and a Kriti.
questions.expectedAnswer: A Geetham is a simple beginner composition, while a Kriti is a more mature composition with greater musical and lyrical depth.

questions.question: State one difference between a Varnam and a Kriti.
questions.expectedAnswer: A Varnam mainly develops raga, voice and rhythmic control, while a Kriti gives greater importance to lyrics, devotion and emotional expression.

questions.question: What are the three main parts of a Kriti?
questions.expectedAnswer: Pallavi, Anupallavi and Charanam.

questions.question: What is the Pallavi of a Kriti?
questions.expectedAnswer: The Pallavi is the opening section and the main musical idea of the Kriti.

questions.question: What is the Anupallavi?
questions.expectedAnswer: The Anupallavi is the section that follows the Pallavi and develops the musical and lyrical idea further.

questions.question: What is the Charanam?
questions.expectedAnswer: The Charanam is the concluding major section of a Kriti and usually contains an expanded lyrical message.

questions.question: Name the four composers included in Grade 8.
questions.expectedAnswer: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri and Purandaradasa.

questions.question: Who was Tyagaraja?
questions.expectedAnswer: Tyagaraja was a great Carnatic composer known especially for devotional compositions.

questions.question: Who was Muthuswami Dikshitar?
questions.expectedAnswer: Muthuswami Dikshitar was a major Carnatic composer known for dignified compositions, many of which were written in Sanskrit.

questions.question: Who was Syama Sastri?
questions.expectedAnswer: Syama Sastri was a major Carnatic composer known for deeply devotional and musically rich compositions.

questions.question: Why is Purandaradasa important in Carnatic music?
questions.expectedAnswer: Purandaradasa made an important contribution to Carnatic music teaching and devotional composition.

questions.question: What does Sahitya mean?
questions.expectedAnswer: Sahitya means the lyrics or words of a musical composition.

questions.question: What is a Sangati?
questions.expectedAnswer: A Sangati is a melodic variation developed from the same lyrical line.

questions.question: Why should students understand the Sahitya before singing a Kriti?
questions.expectedAnswer: Understanding the Sahitya helps students communicate the meaning, devotion and emotion of the composition correctly.

questions.question: What is the difference between word meaning and devotional meaning?
questions.expectedAnswer: Word meaning explains what each word says, while devotional meaning explains the deeper spiritual or emotional message of the lyrics.

questions.question: Why is correct pronunciation important when singing a Kriti?
questions.expectedAnswer: Correct pronunciation preserves the meaning of the lyrics and shows respect for the language and composer.

questions.question: What is a simple Sangati?
questions.expectedAnswer: A simple Sangati is an easy melodic variation of a line without major musical expansion.

questions.question: What is a progressive Sangati?
questions.expectedAnswer: A progressive Sangati is a variation that gradually becomes more developed than the previous version.

questions.question: What is meant by controlled variation in Sangati singing?
questions.expectedAnswer: Controlled variation means singing each Sangati with accuracy, discipline and proper connection to the original line.

questions.question: What is Eduppu?
questions.expectedAnswer: Eduppu is the point at which a composition or musical line begins in relation to the Tala beat.

questions.question: What is Samam Eduppu?
questions.expectedAnswer: Samam Eduppu means that the composition begins exactly on the main beat of the Tala cycle.

questions.question: What is a before-beat Eduppu?
questions.expectedAnswer: It is an entry in which the composition begins before the main beat of the Tala cycle.

questions.question: What is an after-beat Eduppu?
questions.expectedAnswer: It is an entry in which the composition begins after the main beat of the Tala cycle.

questions.question: During a listening exercise, a Kriti begins exactly with the first Tala beat. What type of Eduppu is used?
questions.expectedAnswer: Samam Eduppu.

questions.question: During a listening exercise, the Tala begins first and the singer enters slightly later. What type of Eduppu is used?
questions.expectedAnswer: After-beat Eduppu.

questions.question: What does Bhava mean in Kriti presentation?
questions.expectedAnswer: Bhava means expressing the meaning, feeling and emotional quality of the composition through singing.

questions.question: How can a student show respect for the composer while presenting a Kriti?
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should preserve the composition, pronounce the lyrics correctly, understand the meaning and avoid careless changes.

questions.question: Mention two qualities of a confident Kriti presentation.
questions.expectedAnswer: Steady singing, clear pronunciation, correct lyrics, controlled Sangatis, suitable expression and proper posture. Any two are acceptable.

questions.question: Compare a Geetham, a Varnam and a Kriti according to their main learning purpose.
questions.expectedAnswer: A Geetham introduces simple composition singing. A Varnam develops voice, raga and rhythmic control. A Kriti develops musical maturity, Sahitya understanding, devotion, Sangati and expressive presentation.

questions.question: Explain how the Pallavi, Anupallavi and Charanam help organise a Kriti.
questions.expectedAnswer: The Pallavi introduces the main idea, the Anupallavi develops it, and the Charanam expands or completes the musical and lyrical message.

questions.question: In a listening test, a section is heard after the Pallavi but before the Charanam. Identify the section and explain its function.
questions.expectedAnswer: It is the Anupallavi. It develops the musical and lyrical idea introduced in the Pallavi.

questions.question: A singer repeats the same lyrical line several times, with each repetition becoming more developed. What concept is being demonstrated?
questions.expectedAnswer: Progressive Sangati. The melody is gradually expanded while the lyrical line remains the same.

questions.question: What may happen when a student sings Sangatis without control?
questions.expectedAnswer: The melody may become inaccurate, the lyrics may become unclear, the raga character may be weakened and the composition may lose dignity.

questions.question: Explain how incorrect pronunciation can affect both meaning and Bhava.
questions.expectedAnswer: Incorrect pronunciation can change or confuse the meaning of the words. When the meaning becomes unclear, the correct emotion and devotional message cannot be expressed properly.

questions.question: Describe a simple method for identifying the Eduppu of a Kriti by listening.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should keep the Tala steadily, observe the main beat and listen carefully to whether the song begins on, before or after that beat.

questions.question: Compare Samam, before-beat and after-beat Eduppu.
questions.expectedAnswer: Samam begins on the main beat, before-beat Eduppu begins before it, and after-beat Eduppu begins after it.

questions.question: Explain why a Kriti should not be treated as only a melody.
questions.expectedAnswer: A Kriti contains melody, raga depth, poetry, devotion and meaning. Singing only the notes without understanding the Sahitya and Bhava gives an incomplete presentation.

questions.question: A student sings all the notes correctly but shows no understanding of the words. What should be improved?
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should study the word meaning, devotional message and pronunciation, and then sing with suitable Bhava and dignified expression.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of Kriti in your own words.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should explain that a Kriti is a mature Carnatic composition combining melody, lyrics, devotion, poetry and raga expression.

questions.question: Name and explain the three main sections of a Kriti.
questions.expectedAnswer: Pallavi: opening and main idea. Anupallavi: development of the idea. Charanam: expanded or concluding major section.

questions.question: Name one composer from this grade and explain one basic fact about that composer.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student may name Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri or Purandaradasa and state one accurate basic fact.

questions.question: Choose one line from a Kriti you have learnt. Explain its word meaning and devotional meaning.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should give a clear meaning of the words and explain the emotional or devotional message of the chosen line.

questions.question: Sing or demonstrate one simple Sangati and one progressive Sangati from a Kriti you have learnt.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should sing the basic melodic line first and then a correctly developed variation with control.

questions.question: Demonstrate Samam Eduppu using Tala and a suitable line from a Kriti.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should keep the Tala steadily and begin the line exactly on the main beat.

questions.question: Explain and demonstrate how a before-beat Eduppu works.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should explain that the musical line starts before the main beat and demonstrate the entry correctly with Tala.

questions.question: Explain and demonstrate how an after-beat Eduppu works.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should explain that the Tala begins first and the musical line enters after the main beat.

questions.question: Sing one line of a Kriti with Bhava. Then explain how your expression matches the meaning.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should sing with clear pronunciation, suitable emotion and dignity, and explain the connection between the lyrics and expression.

questions.question: Listen to a short Kriti presentation by the teacher. Identify two strengths or weaknesses related to pronunciation, Sangati, Bhava or confidence.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student should identify two relevant features and explain whether they improve or weaken the presentation.
